profile.name: Mario Cano
profile.title: Senior Software Engineer
profile.summary: Senior Software Engineer at EPAM Systems, delivering full-stack work in JavaScript/TypeScript (React, Node.js) and Python (Django) for enterprise clients including Travelers, Epic Games, Nordstrom, and McKesson. Experienced in cloud-native delivery on AWS and Kubernetes, 24/7 on-call operations, and observability. Started in environmental engineering and hydrology data science at SIATA, the Aburrá Valley Early Warning System, building monitoring, forecasting, and early-alarm systems.

experiences.summary: Senior engineer on enterprise client engagements, owning full-stack delivery with Node.js, React, and AWS.

projects.name: Travelers
projects.subtitle: MuleSoft exit
highlights: Owned several legacy services and led their migration from MuleSoft to Node.js on AWS Lambda, API Gateway, and Express.js.
Built custom Claude skills that standardized and accelerated migration workflows across services.
Added SonarQube, Snyk, and 42Crunch security and quality checks, plus CloudWatch and Dynatrace observability for the migrated services.

projects.name: Epic Games
projects.subtitle: Accounts & Identity
highlights: Frontend lead on the launch of Epic Games Authenticator: MFA and authorization flows in Node.js and React for millions of users.
Defined technical approaches, ran A/B tests on authentication flows, and expanded end-to-end coverage with Playwright and Selenium.
Handled on-call for high-priority production incidents and improved Grafana monitoring with the Telemetry & Analytics team.

projects.name: Nordstrom
projects.subtitle: Product Selling Controls
highlights: Designed and built a NestJS Backend-for-Frontend from scratch, plus React features on Ag-Grid's server-side row model.
Built large-file upload, transformation, and custom Excel export workflows on Node.js and AWS S3.
Migrated complex SQL from Teradata to BigQuery and contributed to Airflow export pipelines.
Shared 24/7 on-call in a 14-person distributed team; Kubernetes, Terraform, Splunk, New Relic.

projects.name: McKesson
projects.subtitle: McKesson Connect ordering platform on SAP Commerce (Hybris)
highlights: Helped move the Item Maintenance page from vanilla JavaScript to React, building its initial Redux Toolkit store and sagas.
Built search and dropdown components to look up products across multiple accounts, and customized editable grid columns.
Integrated Google Analytics 4 events with Hybris promotions and with the Okta login flow.
Unit-tested every delivered feature in Jest and raised overall coverage; contributed to effort estimates and supported the BA in client meetings.

experiences.summary: AI-powered stock market platform: AI models generate trading signals and price forecasts, shown through custom interactive charts.
highlights: Led the frontend team in designing and estimating the company's new AI platform.
Built custom stock market charts in React and TypeScript, and used Next.js server-side rendering to improve SEO and initial load times.
Maintained the Django REST API; reduced AI model loading times with Celery parallel processing and added Redis cache-aside caching.
Integrated Stripe payments and Auth0 authentication; introduced Tailwind CSS to standardize the UI.

experiences.summary: AI-powered demand planning dashboard: AI models generate demand forecasts, presented in interactive charts for business planning.
highlights: Built and maintained the Django REST Framework API serving forecasts, with Celery parallel processing and Redis caching.
Helped migrate the frontend from vanilla JavaScript to React with Redux, and cut bundle size and load times through code splitting.
Contributed to the frontend CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions and Azure.
Integrated Stripe payments and Auth0 authentication.

experiences.summary: Real-time flood forecasting tools and a hydrology application for SIATA, the Aburrá Valley Early Warning System.
highlights: Created a notification service that alerts the city fire department to heavy rainfall, and a web app to trigger community alarms across the valley.
Designed and built a React app for collecting in-situ water flow measurements in the field.
Extended the Django/PostgreSQL data model and REST API to store and serve geometric (GIS) data.
Created an ETL process moving gauging-station data into the Hydrology team's database.
Helped define risk levels for critical points in the drainage basin.

experiences.summary: Web development and hydrological data analysis to improve forecasting, visualization, and real-time reporting at SIATA.
highlights: Designed a Django web app centralizing hydraulic data for the hydrology team, and contributed to the initial models for rainfall, water level, and surface velocity data.
Built a REST API with Django REST Framework and migrated the Django-rendered frontend to React.
Automated environmental image processing with cron jobs and contributed to automated daily and monthly hydrometeorological reports.
Created Matplotlib charts for the data analytics team.

experiences.summary: As part of the hydrology team at SIATA, the Aburrá Valley Early Warning System (Medellín, Colombia), through Universidad EAFIT.
highlights: Set up the monitoring system for the valley's streams and the Medellín River, including telemetry for water level and surface velocity sensors.
Determined station risk levels and built the system that sent early alarms to communities based on each station's risk level during rainfall events.
Built real-time charts and automated reports of rainfall events.
Researched extreme events using hydrological models and statistical water level forecasts, modeling hydrological events with Bayesian networks and Kalman filters.

experiences.summary: On-call operations at SIATA, the Aburrá Valley Early Warning System (Medellín, Colombia), through Universidad EAFIT.
highlights: Provided 24/7 on-call coverage from the command center, reporting in real time on extreme rainfall events and on infrastructure incidents such as database failures.
Triaged incidents and maintained the runbooks used to respond to them.
Sent reports, alerts, and alarm notices to the city entities involved, such as the fire department and local communities.
Kept communication with the stations of the monitoring network and supported the hydrology team's activities.
Worked extensively with Bash, Python, SQL, and monitoring tools during on-call operations.

experiences.summary: Research at CALAIRE (Air Quality Laboratory, Facultad de Minas) under Prof. José Fernando Jiménez, on forecasting critical air pollution episodes in the Aburrá Valley (Medellín, Colombia).
highlights: Developed a feedforward neural network in Python to forecast next-day PM2.5 concentrations and flag critical episodes (daily average above 35 µg/m³).

Derived mixing layer height from vertical temperature and humidity profiles measured by the microwave radiometer (Radiometrics MP-3000A) operated by SIATA, the valley's early warning system, improving knowledge of the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) and using it as a model input.
Combined boundary layer data with surface meteorology (temperature, humidity, solar radiation, precipitation, wind) and previous-day PM2.5 from the valley's air quality network.
Contributed to the research line published in DYNA (2019): "Artificial neural network applied for the forecast of critical PM2.5 events in the Aburra Valley".

experiences.summary: Hydrological and hydraulic analysis supporting the water budget study of the Aburrá Valley (Medellín, Antioquia, Colombia).
highlights: Produced spatial rainfall maps by downscaling large-scale NASA satellite precipitation data (IMERG) and merging it with in situ rain gauge records, combining the spatial coverage of satellite estimates with the accuracy of ground measurements.
Developed stage–discharge rating curves for water level stations, converting level readings into streamflow estimates.
Performed environmental data analysis, processing hydrometeorological datasets with Python (Cython, multiprocessing) and Fortran to support the hydrological and hydraulic studies of the basin.
Fluid Mechanics student assistant in the Hydraulics laboratory, supporting academic activities and laboratory practice.

learning.summary: 62 completed items on LinkedIn Learning: one learning path and 61 courses.
